original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-h1-extensions}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules on $\mathcal{C}$.
There is a canonical bijection
$$
\Ext^1_{\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})}(\mathcal{O}, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
H^1(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})
$$
which associates to the extension
$$
0 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{O} \to 0
$$
the image of $1 \in \Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ in
$H^1(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})$.

final_content.statement:
Here $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal O,\mathcal F)$ is the Yoneda extension group of short exact sequences of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. The group $H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal F)$ is the first right-derived functor of global sections on the ringed site (with $\mathcal F$ regarded as an $\mathcal O$-module). An extension determines the indicated cohomology class by the connecting homomorphism applied to the global unit section $1\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$.

hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.
$\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules.
conclusions: There is a canonical bijection $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal O,\mathcal F)\to H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal F)$ taking the class of $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal O\to0$ to the boundary of $1\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$.

semantic_review_note: For a ringed site and O-module F, the canonical identification Ext^1_{Mod(O)}(O,F)≈H^1(C,F) sends an extension's Yoneda class to the connecting class of the unit section 1, with derived sections taken in the module category. The proposal preserves this precise map.
